stem: The establishment of the wildlife corridors discussed in the excerpt was most likely necessary to prevent —

options.label: A
options.text: the spread of disease among animals

options.label: C
options.text: a rapid increase in the number of animals

options.label: D
options.text: an invasion of non-native animal species

visual_elements: As the human population grows in the Flagstaff region, we increase the impact of transportation corridors (such as roads and rails) and land use changes (such as urban and rural development) on wildlife populations. . . .  To that end, the City of Flagstaff and Coconino County requested wildlife corridor information from the Arizona Game and Fish Department. . . .  —Jessica Gist and Sarah Reif, Arizona Game and Fish Department, August 2009
